   915	/-- The divisor quotient remains epi after tensoring with any module.
   916	
   917	This is the pre-pushforward epimorphism in the D2' evaluation map.  It uses
   918	only the `DivFamily` quotient's existing epimorphism; global generation after
   919	pushforward remains the separate curve-theoretic obligation. -/
   920	theorem twistQuotientMap_epi (L : X.Modules) (x : DivFamily π T) :
   921	    Epi (x.twistQuotientMap L) := by
   922	  letI := x.epi
   923	  haveI : Epi (Modules.tensorObj_functoriality
   924	      (𝟙 ((Modules.pullback (pullback.fst π T.hom)).obj L))
   925	      ((Modules.pullbackUnitIso (pullback.fst π T.hom)).inv ≫ x.q)) :=
   926	    Modules.tensorObj_functoriality_epi_right _
   927	  change Epi ((Modules.tensorObj_right_unitor
   928	    ((Modules.pullback (pullback.fst π T.hom)).obj L)).inv ≫
   929	      Modules.tensorObj_functoriality
   930	        (𝟙 ((Modules.pullback (pullback.fst π T.hom)).obj L))
   931	        ((Modules.pullbackUnitIso (pullback.fst π T.hom)).inv ≫ x.q))
   932	  letI : Epi (Modules.tensorObj_right_unitor
   933	      ((Modules.pullback (pullback.fst π T.hom)).obj L)).inv := inferInstance
   934	  infer_instance

   936	/-- The D2 twist is finitely presented whenever the fixed twist is a line
   937	bundle.  Both antecedents are already produced by the construction: local
   938	triviality survives pullback, and a divisor family carries finite
   939	presentation of its structure module. -/
   940	theorem twist_isFinitePresentation
   941	    (L : X.Modules) (hL : LineBundle.IsLocallyTrivial L)
   942	    (x : DivFamily π T) :
   943	    (x.twist L).IsFinitePresentation := by
   944	  dsimp [twist]
   945	  exact Modules.isFinitePresentation_tensorObj_left_of_isLocallyTrivial _ _
   946	    (hL.pullback (pullback.fst π T.hom)) x.isFinitePresentation
   947	
   948	/-- Quasi-coherence of the D2 twist, obtained from its finite presentation. -/
   949	theorem twist_isQuasicoherent
   950	    (L : X.Modules) (hL : LineBundle.IsLocallyTrivial L)
   951	    (x : DivFamily π T) :
   952	    (x.twist L).IsQuasicoherent := by
   953	  letI : (x.twist L).IsFinitePresentation := x.twist_isFinitePresentation L hL
   954	  infer_instance
   955	
   956	/-- Flatness of the D2 twist over the test base.  This is inherited from the
   957	divisor family's flat structure sheaf through the local line-bundle charts. -/
   958	theorem twist_isCoherentSheafFlat
   959	    (L : X.Modules) (hL : LineBundle.IsLocallyTrivial L)
   960	    (x : DivFamily π T) :
   961	    CoherentSheafFlat (pullback.snd π T.hom) (x.twist L) := by
   962	  dsimp [twist]
   963	  exact Modules.coherentSheafFlat_tensorObj_left_of_isLocallyTrivial
   964	    (pullback.snd π T.hom)
   965	    ((Modules.pullback (pullback.fst π T.hom)).obj L) x.F
   966	    (hL.pullback (pullback.fst π T.hom)) x.isFinitePresentation x.flat
   967	
   968	/-- The D2 twist has proper support whenever the divisor structure sheaf does.
   969	This is unconditional in the twist module: it is the right-factor support
   970	transport, so no rational point, representability, or flatness hypothesis is
   971	introduced here. -/
   972	theorem twist_hasProperSupport (L : X.Modules) (x : DivFamily π T) :
   973	    Modules.HasProperSupport (pullback.snd π T.hom) (x.twist L) := by
   974	  dsimp [twist]
   975	  exact Modules.hasProperSupport_tensorObj_right
   976	    (pullback.snd π T.hom)
   977	    ((Modules.pullback (pullback.fst π T.hom)).obj L) x.properSupport
   978	
   979	/-- Tensoring a divisor module by a line bundle preserves its schematic
   980	support, hence preserves the locally-quasi-finite support condition in both
   981	directions. -/
   982	theorem twist_locallyQuasiFinite_iff
   983	    (L : X.Modules) (hL : LineBundle.IsLocallyTrivial L)
   984	    (x : DivFamily π T) :
   985	    LocallyQuasiFinite
   986	        (Modules.schematicSupportι (x.twist L) ≫ pullback.snd π T.hom) ↔
   987	      LocallyQuasiFinite
   988	        (Modules.schematicSupportι x.F ≫ pullback.snd π T.hom) := by
   989	  dsimp [twist]
   990	  change LocallyQuasiFinite
   991	      ((Modules.annihilator
   992	        (Modules.tensorObj
   993	          ((Modules.pullback (pullback.fst π T.hom)).obj L) x.F)).subschemeι ≫
   994	        pullback.snd π T.hom) ↔
   995	    LocallyQuasiFinite
   996	      ((Modules.annihilator x.F).subschemeι ≫ pullback.snd π T.hom)
   997	  rw [Modules.annihilator_tensorObj_eq_right_of_isLocallyTrivial
   998	    ((Modules.pullback (pullback.fst π T.hom)).obj L) x.F
   999	    (hL.pullback (pullback.fst π T.hom))]
  1000	
  1001	/-- A locally trivial twist has exactly the divisor's annihilator ideal.  Thus
  1002	the D2 target has the same schematic support as the original divisor family,
  1003	not merely a closed subscheme of it. -/
  1004	theorem twist_annihilator_eq_of_isLocallyTrivial
  1005	    (L : X.Modules) (hL : LineBundle.IsLocallyTrivial L)
  1006	    (x : DivFamily π T) :
  1007	    Modules.annihilator (x.twist L) = Modules.annihilator x.F := by
  1008	  dsimp [twist]
  1009	  exact Modules.annihilator_tensorObj_eq_right_of_isLocallyTrivial _ _
  1010	    (hL.pullback (pullback.fst π T.hom))
  1011	
  1012	/-- Finiteness of the schematic support is unchanged by the D2 line-bundle
  1013	twist. -/
  1014	theorem twist_isFiniteSupport_iff
  1015	    (L : X.Modules) (hL : LineBundle.IsLocallyTrivial L)
  1016	    (x : DivFamily π T) :
  1017	    IsFinite (Modules.schematicSupportι (x.twist L) ≫ pullback.snd π T.hom) ↔
  1018	      IsFinite (Modules.schematicSupportι x.F ≫ pullback.snd π T.hom) := by
  1019	  dsimp [twist]
  1020	  exact Modules.isFinite_tensorObj_left_iff
  1021	    (pullback.snd π T.hom)
  1022	    ((Modules.pullback (pullback.fst π T.hom)).obj L) x.F
  1023	    (hL.pullback (pullback.fst π T.hom))
  1024	
  1025	/-- The finite-support producer for the twisted D2 target.  It spends only the
  1026	same locally-quasi-finite support binder already carried by the divisor row;
  1027	properness comes from `DivFamily.properSupport`, and exact support preservation
  1028	then transports finiteness to the twist. -/
  1029	theorem twist_isFiniteSupport
  1030	    (L : X.Modules) (hL : LineBundle.IsLocallyTrivial L)
  1031	    (x : DivFamily π T)
  1032	    [LocallyQuasiFinite
  1033	      (Modules.schematicSupportι x.F ≫ pullback.snd π T.hom)] :
  1034	    IsFinite (Modules.schematicSupportι (x.twist L) ≫ pullback.snd π T.hom) := by
  1035	  rw [twist_isFiniteSupport_iff L hL x]
  1036	  haveI : IsProper
  1037	      (Modules.schematicSupportι x.F ≫ pullback.snd π T.hom) := x.properSupport
  1038	  exact IsFinite.of_isProper_of_locallyQuasiFinite _
  1039	
  1040	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
  1041	/-- On an affine test base, a finite-flat divisor pushforward is locally free
  1042	of the divisor's fibre degree.  The proof supplies finite presentation and
  1043	projectivity from the existing pushforward producers; the rank is computed by
  1044	the finite-support base-change bridge above, not assumed separately.
  1045	
  1046	This is the available affine/noetherian bridge: it still requires the explicit
  1047	`LocallyQuasiFinite` support instance and `[IsNoetherianRing R]`.  It is not yet
  1048	the arbitrary-`Over S` producer for the twisted D2' target. -/
  1049	theorem pushforward_isLocallyFreeOfRank
  1050	    {R : CommRingCat.{u}} {S X : Scheme.{u}} {π : X ⟶ S}
  1051	    [IsProper π] (f : Spec R ⟶ S) [IsNoetherianRing R]
  1052	    (x : DivFamily π (Over.mk f))
  1053	    [LocallyQuasiFinite
  1054	      (Modules.schematicSupportι x.F ≫ pullback.snd π (Over.mk f).hom)]
  1055	    {d : ℕ} (hx : x.HasFiberDeg d) :
  1056	    SheafOfModules.IsLocallyFreeOfRank
  1057	      ((Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd π f)).obj x.F) d := by
  1058	  letI : IsLocallyNoetherian (Over.mk f).left := by
  1059	    change IsLocallyNoetherian (Spec R)
  1060	    infer_instance
  1061	  letI : x.F.IsFinitePresentation := x.isFinitePresentation
  1062	  letI : x.F.IsQuasicoherent := by
  1063	    exact inferInstance
  1064	  let q := pullback.snd π (Over.mk f).hom
  1065	  let M : (Spec R).Modules := (Modules.pushforward q).obj x.F
  1066	  haveI : QuasiCompact q := by
  1067	    dsimp [q]
  1068	    infer_instance
  1069	  haveI : QuasiSeparated q := by
  1070	    dsimp [q]
  1071	    infer_instance
  1072	  haveI : M.IsFinitePresentation := x.isFinitePresentation_pushforward
  1073	  haveI : M.IsQuasicoherent := x.isQuasicoherent_pushforward
  1074	  letI baseM := ((𝟙 (Spec R)) : Spec R ⟶ Spec R).baseSectionsModule M
  1075	    (⊤ : (Spec R).Opens)
  1076	  haveI : IsNoetherianRing Γ(Spec R, (⊤ : (Spec R).Opens)) :=
  1077	    isNoetherianRing_of_ringEquiv R
  1078	      (Scheme.ΓSpecIso R).commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv.symm
  1079	  have hfinΓ : Module.Finite Γ(Spec R, (⊤ : (Spec R).Opens))
  1080	      Γ(M, (⊤ : (Spec R).Opens)) :=
  1081	    Modules.module_finite_sections_of_isFinitePresentation M
  1082	      ⟨⊤, isAffineOpen_top (Spec R)⟩
  1083	  have hfin : Module.Finite R Γ(M, (⊤ : (Spec R).Opens)) :=
  1084	    module_finite_top_of_gammaSpecTop M hfinΓ
  1085	  letI : Module.Finite Γ(Spec R, (⊤ : (Spec R).Opens))
  1086	      Γ(M, (⊤ : (Spec R).Opens)) := hfinΓ
  1087	  have hflatΓ : Module.Flat Γ(Spec R, (⊤ : (Spec R).Opens))
  1088	      Γ(M, (⊤ : (Spec R).Opens)) :=
  1089	    Modules.flat_sections_of_coherentSheafFlat_id
  1090	      x.coherentSheafFlat_id_pushforward (isAffineOpen_top (Spec R))
  1091	  letI : Module.Flat Γ(Spec R, (⊤ : (Spec R).Opens))
  1092	      Γ(M, (⊤ : (Spec R).Opens)) := hflatΓ
  1093	  letI : Module.FinitePresentation Γ(Spec R, (⊤ : (Spec R).Opens))
  1094	      Γ(M, (⊤ : (Spec R).Opens)) :=
  1095	    Module.finitePresentation_of_finite Γ(Spec R, (⊤ : (Spec R).Opens)) _
  1096	  have hprojΓ : Module.Projective Γ(Spec R, (⊤ : (Spec R).Opens))
  1097	      Γ(M, (⊤ : (Spec R).Opens)) :=
  1098	    Module.Flat.projective_of_finitePresentation
  1099	  have hproj : Module.Projective R Γ(M, (⊤ : (Spec R).Opens)) :=
  1100	    module_projective_top_of_gammaSpecTop M hprojΓ
  1101	  letI : Module.Projective R Γ(M, (⊤ : (Spec R).Opens)) := hproj
  1102	  letI : Module.Flat R Γ(M, (⊤ : (Spec R).Opens)) := Module.Flat.of_projective
  1103	  apply Modules.isLocallyFreeOfRank_of_finite_projective_sections M hfin inferInstance
  1104	  intro t
  1105	  change Module.rankAtStalk Γ(M, (⊤ : (Spec R).Opens)) t = d
  1106	  rw [Module.rankAtStalk_eq]
  1107	  haveI : IsProper (Modules.schematicSupportι x.F ≫ q) := x.properSupport
  1108	  have hsupport : IsFinite (Modules.schematicSupportι x.F ≫ q) :=
  1109	    IsFinite.of_isProper_of_locallyQuasiFinite _
  1110	  exact (Modules.fiberRank_gammaTop_eq_fiberH0_of_isFinite_schematicSupport
  1111	    q x.F hsupport t).trans (hx t)

  1143	adding a rational-point binder or another representability class.

  1145	At this mathlib pin `IsProjectiveWith` is Scheme-`0`-valued, so this named
  1146	witness is the small-universe (`k : Type`) route rather than a universe-polymorphic

  1149	    {k : Type} [Field k]
  1150	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))

  1160	    C.hom.IsProjectiveWith (d2ProjectiveTwist C) :=

  1163	theorem d2ProjectiveTwist_isLocallyTrivial
  1164	    {k : Type} [Field k]
  1165	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
  1166	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
  1167	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] :
  1168	    Scheme.LineBundle.IsLocallyTrivial (d2ProjectiveTwist C) := by
  1169	  obtain ⟨n, hn, i, hi, hcomp, ⟨e⟩⟩ :=
  1170	    d2ProjectiveTwist_isProjectiveWith C
  1171	  letI : Finite n := hn
  1172	  exact Scheme.LineBundle.IsLocallyTrivial.of_iso e.symm
  1173	    ((ProjTwist.twistingSheaf_isLocallyTrivial n
  1174	      (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) 1).pullback i)

    17	/-!
    18	# The divisor-to-Grassmannian comparison
    19	
    20	This file begins campaign milestone D2': a divisor family is twisted by a fixed
    21	module on the curve, and the pullback--pushforward base-change map followed by
    22	the divisor quotient gives the canonical evaluation morphism used by the
    23	Grassmannian construction.
    24	
    25	The definitions in the first section are unconditional.  In particular,
    26	`DivFamily.grassmannianEval` exists before the Riemann--Roch argument proves it
    27	epimorphic.  Keeping the map separate from its eventual `Epi` proof prevents
    28	uniform generation from becoming an assumption in the definition of the
    29	comparison.
    30	
    31	The second section records two affine algebra bridges used to turn finite flat
    32	pushforwards into the rank-indexed local-freeness predicate expected by
    33	`Scheme.LocallyFreeQuotient`.  They do not introduce a representability gate:
    34	their inputs are ordinary finite-presentation, finiteness, and projectivity
    35	properties with producers elsewhere in the Picard development.
    36	-/
    37	
    38	set_option autoImplicit false
    39	
    40	universe u
    41	
    42	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory
    43	
    44	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    45

    50	variable {S X : Scheme.{u}} {π : X ⟶ S} {T : Over S}
    51	
    52	private lemma map_tensorHom_comp2 {C D : Type*} [Category C] [MonoidalCategory C]
    53	    [Category D] (F : C ⥤ D) {a₀ a₁ a₂ b₀ b₁ b₂ : C}
    54	    (a : a₀ ⟶ a₁) (b : a₁ ⟶ a₂) (d : b₀ ⟶ b₁) (e : b₁ ⟶ b₂) :
    55	    F.map (MonoidalCategory.tensorHom a d) ≫ F.map (MonoidalCategory.tensorHom b e) =
    56	      F.map (MonoidalCategory.tensorHom (a ≫ b) (d ≫ e)) := by
    57	  rw [← F.map_comp, MonoidalCategory.tensorHom_comp_tensorHom]
    58	
    59	/-- The twist of the divisor structure sheaf by a module on the original
    60	family.  For the D2' embedding, `L` is the chosen sufficiently positive
    61	projective twist. -/
    62	noncomputable def twist (L : X.Modules) (x : DivFamily π T) :
    63	    (pullback π T.hom).Modules :=
    64	  Modules.tensorObj ((Modules.pullback (pullback.fst π T.hom)).obj L) x.F
    65	
    66	/-- Tensor the divisor quotient `O -> O_D` with the pulled-back twist. -/
    67	noncomputable def twistQuotientMap (L : X.Modules) (x : DivFamily π T) :
    68	    (Modules.pullback (pullback.fst π T.hom)).obj L ⟶ x.twist L :=
    69	  (Modules.tensorObj_right_unitor _).inv ≫
    70	    Modules.tensorObj_functoriality (𝟙 _)
    71	      ((Modules.pullbackUnitIso (pullback.fst π T.hom)).inv ≫ x.q)
    72	
    73	/-- Equivalent divisor families have isomorphic twists, compatibly with the
    74	twisted quotient maps.  This is the representative-level descent input for
    75	the D2' Grassmannian comparison. -/
    76	lemma twistQuotientMap_rel (L : X.Modules) {x y : DivFamily π T} (h : x.Rel y) :
    77	    ∃ f : x.twist L ≅ y.twist L,
    78	      x.twistQuotientMap L ≫ f.hom = y.twistQuotientMap L := by
    79	  obtain ⟨f, hf⟩ := h
    80	  refine ⟨Modules.tensorObjIsoOfIso (Iso.refl _) f, ?_⟩
    81	  change ((Modules.tensorObj_right_unitor _).inv ≫
    82	      Modules.tensorObj_functoriality (𝟙 _)
    83	        ((Modules.pullbackUnitIso (pullback.fst π T.hom)).inv ≫ x.q)) ≫
    84	      Modules.tensorObj_functoriality (𝟙 _) f.hom =
    85	    (Modules.tensorObj_right_unitor _).inv ≫
    86	      Modules.tensorObj_functoriality (𝟙 _)
    87	        ((Modules.pullbackUnitIso (pullback.fst π T.hom)).inv ≫ y.q)
    88	  rw [Category.assoc]
    89	  rw [show Modules.tensorObj_functoriality (𝟙 _) _ ≫
    90	        Modules.tensorObj_functoriality (𝟙 _) f.hom =
    91	      Modules.tensorObj_functoriality ((𝟙 _) ≫ (𝟙 _))
    92	        (((Modules.pullbackUnitIso (pullback.fst π T.hom)).inv ≫ x.q) ≫ f.hom) by
    93	    simp only [Modules.tensorObj_functoriality]
    94	    exact map_tensorHom_comp2
    95	      (C := _root_.PresheafOfModules
    96	        ((pullback π T.hom).presheaf ⋙ forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat))
    97	      _ _ _ _ _]
    98	  simp only [Category.id_comp]
    99	  rw [Category.assoc, hf]
   100	
   101	/-- The canonical D2' evaluation morphism.
   102	
   103	It first base-changes `π_* L` from `S` to `T`, then pushes forward the twisted
   104	divisor quotient along `X_T -> T`.  Uniform Riemann--Roch will prove that this
   105	map is an epimorphism for a sufficiently positive `L`; no such conclusion is
   106	built into the definition. -/
   107	noncomputable def grassmannianEval (L : X.Modules) (x : DivFamily π T) :
   108	    (Modules.pullback T.hom).obj ((Modules.pushforward π).obj L) ⟶
   109	      (Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd π T.hom)).obj (x.twist L) :=
   110	  pushforwardBaseChangeMap π T.hom (pullback.snd π T.hom)
   111	      (pullback.fst π T.hom) pullback.condition L ≫
   112	    (Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd π T.hom)).map (x.twistQuotientMap L)
   113	
   114	/-- Equivalent divisor families have isomorphic evaluation targets, and the
   115	isomorphism commutes with the D2' evaluation maps. -/
   116	lemma grassmannianEval_rel (L : X.Modules) {x y : DivFamily π T} (h : x.Rel y) :
   117	    ∃ f : (Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd π T.hom)).obj (x.twist L) ≅
   118	        (Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd π T.hom)).obj (y.twist L),
   119	      x.grassmannianEval L ≫ f.hom = y.grassmannianEval L := by

   123	      (pullback.fst π T.hom) pullback.condition L ≫
   124	        (Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd π T.hom)).map (x.twistQuotientMap L)) ≫

   127	      (pullback.fst π T.hom) pullback.condition L ≫

   131	/-- Epimorphy of the D2' evaluation map is invariant under
   132	`DivFamily.Rel`. -/
   133	lemma grassmannianEval_epi_of_rel (L : X.Modules) {x y : DivFamily π T}
   134	    (h : x.Rel y) (hx : Epi (x.grassmannianEval L)) :
   135	    Epi (y.grassmannianEval L) := by
   136	  obtain ⟨f, hf⟩ := grassmannianEval_rel L h

   138	  rw [← hf]
   139	  infer_instance

   142	invariant under `DivFamily.Rel`. -/
   143	lemma grassmannianTarget_isLocallyFreeOfRank_of_rel
   144	    (L : X.Modules) {x y : DivFamily π T} (hxy : x.Rel y) {d : ℕ}
   145	    (hx : SheafOfModules.IsLocallyFreeOfRank
   146	      ((Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd π T.hom)).obj (x.twist L)) d) :
   147	    SheafOfModules.IsLocallyFreeOfRank
   148	      ((Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd π T.hom)).obj (y.twist L)) d := by
   149	  obtain ⟨f, _⟩ := grassmannianEval_rel L hxy
   150	  obtain ⟨ι, U, hU, hloc⟩ := hx
   151	  exact ⟨ι, U, hU, fun i =>
   152	    ⟨(Modules.pullback (U i).ι).mapIso f.symm ≪≫ (hloc i).some⟩⟩
   153	
   154	/-- The evaluation map is epi as soon as its two displayed factors are epi.
   155	This keeps the base-change and divisor-quotient obligations separate, so a
   156	later uniform-generation proof can discharge only the factor it actually
   157	proves. -/
   158	theorem grassmannianEval_epi (L : X.Modules) (x : DivFamily π T)
   159	    (hbase : Epi (pushforwardBaseChangeMap π T.hom
   160	      (pullback.snd π T.hom) (pullback.fst π T.hom) pullback.condition L))
   161	    (hquot : Epi ((Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd π T.hom)).map
   162	      (x.twistQuotientMap L))) :
   163	    Epi (x.grassmannianEval L) := by
   164	  letI := hbase
   165	  letI := hquot
   166	  dsimp [grassmannianEval]
   167	  infer_instance
   168	
   169	/-- **The conditional D2' quotient datum.**  Once the evaluation map is an
   170	epimorphism and its target has constant locally-free rank `d`, it is exactly a
   171	rank-`d` locally free quotient of the pulled-back pushforward of `L`.
   172	
   173	The two arguments are deliberately explicit: the evaluation map is the
   174	uniform-generation obligation, while the locally-free target is the
   175	finite/projective/rank obligation.  This constructor packages those genuine
   176	outputs without introducing a class or an instance that could hide either one.
   177	-/
   178	noncomputable def grassmannianQuotient (L : X.Modules) (x : DivFamily π T)
   179	    [IsLocallyNoetherian S] {d : ℕ} (hEpi : Epi (x.grassmannianEval L))
   180	    (hLocFree : SheafOfModules.IsLocallyFreeOfRank
   181	      ((Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd π T.hom)).obj (x.twist L)) d) :
   182	    LocallyFreeQuotient ((Modules.pushforward π).obj L) d T := by
   183	  letI := hEpi
   184	  exact {
   185	    F := (Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd π T.hom)).obj (x.twist L)
   186	    q := x.grassmannianEval L
   187	    epi := inferInstance
   188	    locFree := hLocFree }
   189	
   190	/-- The conditional D2' quotient datum respects the divisor-family
   191	equivalence relation.  The epi and rank witnesses on the second representative
   192	are transported from the first, rather than assumed again. -/
   193	lemma grassmannianQuotient_rel
   194	    (L : X.Modules) {x y : DivFamily π T} [IsLocallyNoetherian S] {d : ℕ}
   195	    (hxy : x.Rel y) (hxEpi : Epi (x.grassmannianEval L))
   196	    (hxLocFree : SheafOfModules.IsLocallyFreeOfRank
   197	      ((Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd π T.hom)).obj (x.twist L)) d) :
   198	    (grassmannianQuotient L x hxEpi hxLocFree).Rel
   199	      (grassmannianQuotient L y
   200	        (grassmannianEval_epi_of_rel L hxy hxEpi)
   201	        (grassmannianTarget_isLocallyFreeOfRank_of_rel L hxy hxLocFree)) := by
   202	  obtain ⟨f, hf⟩ := grassmannianEval_rel L hxy
   203	  exact ⟨f, hf⟩
   204	
   205	/-- The quotient-class value of the D2' comparison in the relative
   206	Grassmannian functor.  This is the representation-facing object consumed by
   207	the Grassmannian representability theorem; well-definedness under
   208	`DivFamily.Rel` is a separate comparison lemma. -/
   209	noncomputable def grassmannianClass (L : X.Modules) (x : DivFamily π T)
   210	    [IsLocallyNoetherian S] {d : ℕ} (hEpi : Epi (x.grassmannianEval L))
   211	    (hLocFree : SheafOfModules.IsLocallyFreeOfRank
   212	      ((Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd π T.hom)).obj (x.twist L)) d) :
   213	    (Grassmannian ((Modules.pushforward π).obj L) d).obj (Opposite.op T) :=
   214	  Quotient.mk _ (grassmannianQuotient L x hEpi hLocFree)
   215	
   216	/-- The D2' Grassmannian class is well-defined on `DivFamily.Rel`.  Both
   217	analytic obligations are transported along the relation witness, so this
   218	descent theorem introduces no additional hypotheses. -/
   219	theorem grassmannianClass_eq_of_rel
   220	    (L : X.Modules) {x y : DivFamily π T} [IsLocallyNoetherian S] {d : ℕ}
   221	    (hxy : x.Rel y) (hxEpi : Epi (x.grassmannianEval L))
   222	    (hxLocFree : SheafOfModules.IsLocallyFreeOfRank
   223	      ((Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd π T.hom)).obj (x.twist L)) d) :
   224	    grassmannianClass L x hxEpi hxLocFree =
   225	      grassmannianClass L y
   226	        (grassmannianEval_epi_of_rel L hxy hxEpi)
   227	        (grassmannianTarget_isLocallyFreeOfRank_of_rel L hxy hxLocFree) :=
   228	  Quotient.sound (grassmannianQuotient_rel L hxy hxEpi hxLocFree)
   229	
   230	/-- The componentwise form of `grassmannianClass`: once the base-change and
   231	divisor-quotient factors are epi, only the target's rank condition remains. -/
   232	noncomputable def grassmannianClassOfComponents (L : X.Modules) (x : DivFamily π T)
   233	    [IsLocallyNoetherian S] {d : ℕ}
   234	    (hbase : Epi (pushforwardBaseChangeMap π T.hom
   235	      (pullback.snd π T.hom) (pullback.fst π T.hom) pullback.condition L))
   236	    (hquot : Epi ((Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd π T.hom)).map
   237	      (x.twistQuotientMap L)))
   238	    (hLocFree : SheafOfModules.IsLocallyFreeOfRank
   239	      ((Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd π T.hom)).obj (x.twist L)) d) :
   240	    (Grassmannian ((Modules.pushforward π).obj L) d).obj (Opposite.op T) :=
   241	  grassmannianClass L x (grassmannianEval_epi L x hbase hquot) hLocFree
   242

informal/pic-representability-campaign.md:214:**Best ideas to graft**: the audit discipline (arbitrary-`T` quantification; `GeometricallyIntegral` fibre semantics; `Limits.pullback` vs pointwise; Grassmannian quotient-convention — which I verified: `QuotFunctorDef.lean:1076-1092` defines `Grassmannian V d` via rank-`d` locally free **quotients**, the Grothendieck `P(E)` convention); the `C^d` universal-divisor-family trick (M7) as a duality-free fallback for uniform vanishing; increasing-union separatedness (not needed on the winning route but sound).

informal/pic-representability-campaign.md:218:**Sound** (7.5): right architecture (Milne–Kollár + finite Galois quotient); explicit `M0` (universal H⁰), Γ-stable common-Σ refinement, and char-p separability care are the best-worked Galois details of the three. Deductions: M12 separatedness via the valuative criterion is self-flagged risky (mathlib's criterion quantifies over ALL valuation rings, `ValuativeCriterion.lean:245`, vs the noetherian-pinned M1 engine; DVR-sufficiency is an acknowledged mathlib TODO) — and it is **unnecessary** (see B6 below); M3's suggested proof routes include Serre duality (scope-creep risk D3 correctly avoids).
informal/pic-representability-campaign.md:227:1. **Separatedness of `J'_r` is asserted in J5 but never milestoned.** Gluing the `J^Σ` along nontrivial transition isos does not give separatedness for free; it needs closedness of the transition graphs = closedness of the class-agreement locus. Repaired by the new milestone **B6** (closed-triviality-locus device), which is cheaper and safer than D2's valuative route.
informal/pic-representability-campaign.md:228:2. **G2's hypothesis "immersion `X' ↪ ℙ^N`" may be unavailable for the *glued* `J'_r`** — a scheme glued from finitely many quasi-projective opens is not obviously quasi-projective, and proving it would smuggle in the ample-bundle problem the Milne route dodges. Repaired by D2's form of the hypothesis: *every finite Γ-orbit lies in an affine open*, supplied by the Γ-stable cover `V_Σ` whose members carry Gr-immersions (finite point-set in a quasi-projective scheme lies in an affine open).
informal/pic-representability-campaign.md:230:**Feasibility 8.5 / Effort 8 / Risk 8.5**: maximal reuse of verified substrate (adelic `RiemannRoch/` lane — verified this session: the only genuine sorry in the lane is `WeilDivisor.principal_degree_zero`; the `Cokernel.lean:133` / `CechAcyclicInstance.lean:73` grep hits are docstring text; plus `DivFunctor` `DivFunctorDef.lean:875`, `Grassmannian.representable` `GrassmannianRepresentability.lean:595-599`, mathlib coproducts `AlgebraicGeometry/Limits.lean:187/:224` (verified: `HasColimitsOfShape (Discrete σ) Scheme.{u}` + `CoproductsOfShapeDisjoint`), 01JJ `Sites/Representability.lean:207`, `sigmaDesc` `Morphisms/Basic.lean:303`, equalizer-closed `Morphisms/Separated.lean:356`). /-!
# The universal locally closed rank locus

This file upgrades the matrix-defined flattening stratum from flatness to the
rank-indexed local-freeness predicate used by the Grassmannian construction.
In rank one it is therefore the universal locally closed locus on which the
module becomes an invertible sheaf.

The construction is unconditional.  It uses the existing presentation charts
and their entry-ideal strata; it does not assume Picard representability or a
rational point.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u

open CategoryTheory Limits

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

namespace Scheme

namespace Modules

variable {X : Scheme.{u}}

/-- An explicit rank-`e` basis of sections on an affine open trivialises the
corresponding restriction of a quasi-coherent module. -/
theorem pullback_isFreeOfRank_of_sectionsEquiv
    (M : X.Modules) [M.IsQuasicoherent] {U : X.Opens} (hU : IsAffineOpen U)
    (e : ℕ) (E : (Fin e → Γ(X, U)) ≃ₗ[Γ(X, U)] Γ(M, U)) :
    Nonempty ((pullback U.ι).obj M ≅
      SheafOfModules.free (R := U.toScheme.ringCatSheaf) (ULift.{u} (Fin e))) := by
  let N := (pullback hU.fromSpec).obj M
  haveI : N.IsQuasicoherent := pullback_isQuasicoherent_hom hU.fromSpec M inferInstance
  haveI : IsIso (fromSpecRestrictTopHom M hU) :=
    fromSpecRestrictTopHom_isIso M hU
  haveI : IsIso ((restrictFunctorIsoPullback hU.fromSpec).hom.app M) := inferInstance
  haveI : IsIso
      (moduleSpecΓFunctor.map ((restrictFunctorIsoPullback hU.fromSpec).hom.app M)) :=
    inferInstance
  let sectionHom : ModuleCat.of Γ(X, U) Γ(M, U) ⟶ moduleSpecΓFunctor.obj N :=
    fromSpecRestrictTopHom M hU ≫
      moduleSpecΓFunctor.map ((restrictFunctorIsoPullback hU.fromSpec).hom.app M)
  haveI : IsIso sectionHom := by
    dsimp only [sectionHom]
    exact IsIso.comp_isIso' (fromSpecRestrictTopHom_isIso M hU) inferInstance
  haveI : IsIso N.fromTildeΓ := isIso_fromTildeΓ_of_isQuasicoherent N
  let eIndex : (ULift.{u} (Fin e) →₀ Γ(X, U)) ≃ₗ[Γ(X, U)] (Fin e → Γ(X, U)) :=
    (Finsupp.linearEquivFunOnFinite Γ(X, U) Γ(X, U) (ULift.{u} (Fin e))).trans
      (LinearEquiv.funCongrLeft Γ(X, U) Γ(X, U) Equiv.ulift.symm)
  let eSections : (ULift.{u} (Fin e) →₀ Γ(X, U)) ≃ₗ[Γ(X, U)]
      moduleSpecΓFunctor.obj N :=
    eIndex.trans (E.trans (asIso sectionHom).toLinearEquiv)
  let eSpec : N ≅
      SheafOfModules.free (R := (Spec Γ(X, U)).ringCatSheaf) (ULift.{u} (Fin e)) :=
    qcoh_iso_tilde_sections N ≪≫
      (tilde.functor Γ(X, U)).mapIso eSections.toModuleIso.symm ≪≫
      tildeFinsupp (ULift.{u} (Fin e))
  have hcomp : hU.isoSpec.hom ≫ hU.fromSpec = U.ι := by
    rw [← hU.isoSpec_inv_ι, Iso.hom_inv_id_assoc]
  exact ⟨
    ((pullbackCongr hcomp).symm.app M) ≪≫
      ((pullbackComp hU.isoSpec.hom hU.fromSpec).app M).symm ≪≫
      (pullback hU.isoSpec.hom).mapIso eSpec ≪≫
      pullbackFreeIso hU.isoSpec.hom (ULift.{u} (Fin e))⟩

/-- The entry-ideal stratum is locally free of its prescribed rank.  This is
the locally-free strengthening of `coherentSheafFlat_stratum`. -/
theorem stratum_isLocallyFreeOfRank
    (M : X.Modules) [M.IsQuasicoherent] {e : ℕ} (hcov : ChartsCover M e) :
    SheafOfModules.IsLocallyFreeOfRank
      ((pullback (stratumι M e hcov)).obj M) e := by
  let N := (pullback (stratumι M e hcov)).obj M
  haveI : N.IsQuasicoherent :=
    pullback_isQuasicoherent_hom (stratumι M e hcov) M inferInstance
  let I := {V : X.affineOpens // IsPresentationChart M e V}
  let W : I → (stratum M e hcov).Opens := fun j =>
    stratumι M e hcov ⁻¹ᵁ j.1.1
  refine ⟨I, W, ?_, fun j => ?_⟩
  · rw [eq_top_iff]
    intro z _
    obtain ⟨V, hzV, hchart⟩ := hcov ((stratumι M e hcov).base z)
    exact TopologicalSpace.Opens.mem_iSup.mpr ⟨⟨V, hchart⟩, hzV⟩
  · obtain ⟨mm, ⟨P⟩⟩ := j.2
    have hW : IsAffineOpen (W j) :=
      j.1.2.preimage (stratumι M e hcov)
    obtain ⟨P', hP'⟩ := exists_matrixPresentation_pullback_sections
      (stratumι M e hcov) M j.1.2 hW le_rfl P
    have h0 : P'.relMatrix = 0 := by
      rw [hP']
      ext a b
      simp only [Matrix.map_apply, Matrix.zero_apply]
      have hmem : ((stratumι M e hcov).app j.1.1).hom (P.relMatrix a b) = 0 := by
        have hker : P.relMatrix a b ∈
            RingHom.ker (((strataData M e hcov).subschemeι.app j.1.1).hom) := by
          rw [Scheme.IdealSheafData.ker_subschemeι_app]
          change P.relMatrix a b ∈ strataIdeal M e j.1
          rw [strataIdeal_eq_entryIdeal M P]
          exact P.relMatrix_mem_entryIdeal a b
        exact RingHom.mem_ker.mp hker
      change ((stratumι M e hcov).appLE j.1.1 (W j) le_rfl).hom
          (P.relMatrix a b) = 0
      have happ : ((stratumι M e hcov).appLE j.1.1 (W j) le_rfl).hom
          (P.relMatrix a b) =
          ((stratum M e hcov).presheaf.map (homOfLE le_rfl).op).hom
            (((stratumι M e hcov).app j.1.1).hom (P.relMatrix a b)) := rfl
      rw [happ, hmem, map_zero]
    exact pullback_isFreeOfRank_of_sectionsEquiv N hW e (P'.projEquiv h0)

/-- Rank-indexed local freeness transports along an isomorphism of module
sheaves, in arbitrary universe. -/
theorem isLocallyFreeOfRank_of_iso_general {M N : X.Modules} (E : M ≅ N)
    {e : ℕ} (hN : SheafOfModules.IsLocallyFreeOfRank N e) :
    SheafOfModules.IsLocallyFreeOfRank M e := by
  obtain ⟨I, U, hU, hfree⟩ := hN
  exact ⟨I, U, hU, fun i => ⟨(pullback (U i).ι).mapIso E ≪≫ (hfree i).some⟩⟩

/-- The canonical locally closed rank stratum carries a locally free module
of exactly the indexed rank. -/
theorem rankStratum_isLocallyFreeOfRank {S : Scheme.{u}}
    (F : S.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] (e : ℕ) :
    SheafOfModules.IsLocallyFreeOfRank
      ((pullback (rankStratumι F e)).obj F) e := by
  let G := (pullback (chartLocus F e).ι).obj F
  haveI : G.IsQuasicoherent :=
    pullback_isQuasicoherent_hom (chartLocus F e).ι F inferInstance
  let hcov : ChartsCover G e := chartsCover_chartLocus F e
  have hfree := stratum_isLocallyFreeOfRank G hcov
  let E : (pullback (rankStratumι F e)).obj F ≅
      (pullback (stratumι G e hcov)).obj G :=
    ((pullbackComp (stratumι G e hcov) (chartLocus F e).ι).app F).symm
  exact isLocallyFreeOfRank_of_iso_general E hfree

/-- The locally closed locus on which a module has rank one. -/
noncomputable abbrev lineBundleLocus {S : Scheme.{u}} (F : S.Modules)
    [F.IsQuasicoherent] : Scheme.{u} :=
  rankStratum F 1

/-- The immersion of the rank-one locus into its base. -/
noncomputable abbrev lineBundleLocusι {S : Scheme.{u}} (F : S.Modules)
    [F.IsQuasicoherent] : lineBundleLocus F ⟶ S :=
  rankStratumι F 1

instance {S : Scheme.{u}} (F : S.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] :
    IsImmersion (lineBundleLocusι F) := inferInstance

/-- The support of the rank-one locus is exactly the point-rank-one set. -/
theorem mem_range_lineBundleLocusι_iff {S : Scheme.{u}}
    [IsLocallyNoetherian S] (F : S.Modules) [F.IsFinitePresentation] (s : S) :
    s ∈ Set.range (lineBundleLocusι F).base ↔ pointRank S F s = 1 :=
  mem_range_rankStratumι_iff F 1 s

/-- On the rank-one locus the pulled-back module is an invertible sheaf. -/
theorem lineBundleLocus_isLocallyTrivial {S : Scheme.{u}}
    (F : S.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] :
    LineBundle.IsLocallyTrivial
      ((pullback (lineBundleLocusι F)).obj F) := by
  obtain ⟨I, U, hU, hfree⟩ := rankStratum_isLocallyFreeOfRank F 1
  apply LineBundle.isLocallyTrivial_of_pointwise_free_one
  intro x
  have hx : x ∈ ⨆ i, U i := by rw [hU]; trivial
  obtain ⟨i, hxi⟩ := TopologicalSpace.Opens.mem_iSup.mp hx
  exact ⟨U i, hxi, hfree i⟩

/-- A locally trivial line bundle is flat over its base.  This is the
representation-facing form of the chart-local flatness recorded by
`LineBundle.IsLocallyTrivial`: on a trivialising affine chart its section
module is linearly equivalent to the coordinate ring. -/
theorem coherentSheafFlat_id_of_isLocallyTrivial {S : Scheme.{u}}
    {F : S.Modules} (hF : LineBundle.IsLocallyTrivial F) :
    Scheme.CoherentSheafFlat (𝟙 S) F := by
  haveI : F.IsFinitePresentation := hF.isFinitePresentation
  obtain ⟨I, U, hUaff, hUtop, hUiso⟩ := hF.exists_trivializing_cover
  apply coherentSheafFlat_id_of_charts F U hUaff
  · intro s
    have hs : s ∈ iSup U := by rw [hUtop]; trivial
    exact TopologicalSpace.Opens.mem_iSup.mp hs
  · intro i
    let eRes : F.restrict (U i).ι ≅
        (restrictFunctor (U i).ι).obj
          (SheafOfModules.unit S.ringCatSheaf) :=
      (hUiso i).some ≪≫
        ((restrictFunctorIsoPullback (U i).ι).app
          (SheafOfModules.unit S.ringCatSheaf) ≪≫ pullbackUnitIso (U i).ι).symm
    let eΓ : Γ(F, U i) ≃ₗ[Γ(S, U i)] Γ(S, U i) :=
      sectionLinearEquivOfRestrictIso (U i) eRes
    exact Module.Flat.of_linearEquiv (M := Γ(S, U i)) eΓ

/-- Every fibre of a locally trivial line bundle has dimension one. -/
theorem pointRank_eq_one_of_isLocallyTrivial {S : Scheme.{u}}
    {F : S.Modules} [F.IsQuasicoherent]
    (hF : LineBundle.IsLocallyTrivial F) (s : S) :
    pointRank S F s = 1 := by
  obtain ⟨U, hsU, hUaff, ⟨eU⟩⟩ := hF s
  let V : S.affineOpens := ⟨U, hUaff⟩
  have hsV : s ∈ V.1 := hsU
  rw [pointRank_eq_chartFiberRank F (V := V) s hsV]
  let p : PrimeSpectrum Γ(S, U) := hUaff.primeIdealOf ⟨s, hsU⟩
  haveI : Nontrivial Γ(S, U) := PrimeSpectrum.nontrivial p
  change p.asIdeal.fiberRank Γ(F, U) = 1
  let eRes : F.restrict U.ι ≅
      (restrictFunctor U.ι).obj (SheafOfModules.unit S.ringCatSheaf) :=
    eU ≪≫ ((restrictFunctorIsoPullback U.ι).app
      (SheafOfModules.unit S.ringCatSheaf) ≪≫ pullbackUnitIso U.ι).symm
  let eΓ : Γ(F, U) ≃ₗ[Γ(S, U)] Γ(S, U) :=
    sectionLinearEquivOfRestrictIso U eRes
  rw [Ideal.fiberRank_congr _ eΓ]
  exact (Ideal.finrank_fiber_eq_rankAtStalk _).trans
    (congrFun (Module.rankAtStalk_self (R := Γ(S, U))) p)

/-- Universal factorisation through the locally closed rank-one locus.  The
antecedent is the existing flattening condition: flat pullback with constant
point rank one. -/
theorem existsUnique_factor_lineBundleLocus {S : Scheme.{u}}
    [IsLocallyNoetherian S] (F : S.Modules) [F.IsFinitePresentation]
    {T : Scheme.{u}} (φ : T ⟶ S)
    (hflat : Scheme.CoherentSheafFlat (𝟙 T) ((pullback φ).obj F))
    (hrank : ∀ t : T, pointRank S F (φ.base t) = 1) :
    ∃! l : T ⟶ lineBundleLocus F, l ≫ lineBundleLocusι F = φ :=
  existsUnique_factor_rankStratum F 1 φ hflat hrank

/-- Universal factorisation through the line-bundle locus, stated only in
terms of the predicate represented by that locus.  Local triviality of the
pullback supplies both flatness and constant fibre rank one. -/
theorem existsUnique_factor_lineBundleLocus_of_isLocallyTrivial
    {S : Scheme.{u}} [IsLocallyNoetherian S]
    (F : S.Modules) [F.IsFinitePresentation]
    {T : Scheme.{u}} (φ : T ⟶ S)
    (hline : LineBundle.IsLocallyTrivial ((pullback φ).obj F)) :
    ∃! l : T ⟶ lineBundleLocus F, l ≫ lineBundleLocusι F = φ := by
  haveI : ((pullback φ).obj F).IsQuasicoherent :=
    pullback_isQuasicoherent_hom φ F inferInstance
  apply existsUnique_factor_lineBundleLocus F φ
    (coherentSheafFlat_id_of_isLocallyTrivial hline)
  intro t
  rw [← pointRank_pullback φ F t]
  exact pointRank_eq_one_of_isLocallyTrivial hline t

# Representability of the relative Grassmannian (`thm:grassmannian_representable`)

This file states and attacks the representability of the relative Grassmannian
functor `Grass(V, d) : (Sch/S)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type 1` (`Scheme.Grassmannian`,
`QuotFunctorDef.lean`) by an `S`-scheme, for `V` a locally free
`O_S`-module of rank `r` and `1 ≤ d ≤ r` ([Nitsure] §1, Exercise (2);
blueprint `thm:grassmannian_representable`).

The statement here **corrects** the earlier skeleton of `QuotFunctorDef.lean`,
which quantified over an arbitrary sheaf of modules `V` with no rank data:
that form is not the [Nitsure] theorem (whose hypotheses are `V` locally free
of rank `r ≥ d ≥ 1`) and is not known to be true for non-quasi-coherent `V`.
The universe is pinned to `Scheme.{0}`: the merged absolute chart construction
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Grassmannian.scheme` / `.represents`,
`GrassmannianQuot.lean`) lives over the genuinely terminal `Spec ℤ` of
`Scheme.{0}`, and the relative theorem is obtained from it.

## Contents

* `Scheme.LocallyFreeQuotient.congrModule` / `Scheme.Grassmannian.congrIso` —
  transport of the Grassmannian functor along an isomorphism `V ≅ V'` of the
  classified module (pure functoriality, no pseudofunctor coherence).
* `Scheme.LocallyFreeQuotient.toRankQuotient` / `.ofRankQuotient` /
  `Scheme.Grassmannian.freeCompare` — for the free module `V = O_S^r`, the
  comparison `Grass(O_S^r, d) ≅ (Over.forget S)ᵒᵖ ⋙ Grass(r, d)` with the
  merged absolute Grassmannian functor, re-presenting the pulled-back free
  module through `Scheme.Modules.pullbackFreeIso`.  Naturality is the free
  coherence `pullbackFreeIso_comp` of `GlueDescent.lean`.
* `Scheme.Grassmannian.prodRepresentableBy` — the absolute Grassmannian,
  pulled back to `Over S` along the forgetful functor, is representable by
  the product `S ⨯ Gr(d, r)` with its first projection (`Spec ℤ` is terminal
  in `Scheme.{0}`, so the product is the base change of `Gr(d, r)` to `S`).
* `Scheme.Grassmannian.representable_of_iso_free` — representability of
  `Grass(V, d)` for globally trivialised `V ≅ O_S^r` (complete proof).
* `Scheme.Grassmannian.representable` — the [Nitsure] statement, for `V`
  locally free of rank `r`: glue `representable_of_iso_free` over a
  trivialising cover of `(S, V)` by Zariski descent of representability
  (`Scheme.representable_of_openCover`, proved in
  `ZariskiDescentRepresentability.lean`); the remaining leaf is the sheaf
  axiom `Grassmannian.isZariskiSheaf`.

/-! ## §1. Transport along an isomorphism of the classified module -/

namespace LocallyFreeQuotient

variable {S : Scheme.{u}} [IsLocallyNoetherian S]

/-- Transport of a rank-`d` locally free quotient of `V'_T` along an
isomorphism `g : V ≅ V'` of the classified modules: precompose the quotient
map with the pulled-back isomorphism.  Underlies the invariance
`Scheme.Grassmannian.congrIso` of the Grassmannian functor. -/
noncomputable def congrModule {V V' : S.Modules} (g : V ≅ V') {d : ℕ} {T : Over S}
    (x : LocallyFreeQuotient V d T) : LocallyFreeQuotient V' d T where
  F := x.F
  q := ((Scheme.Modules.pullback T.hom).mapIso g).inv ≫ x.q
  epi :=
    @CategoryTheory.epi_comp _ _ _ _ _
      ((Scheme.Modules.pullback T.hom).mapIso g).inv inferInstance
      x.q x.epi
  locFree := x.locFree

omit [IsLocallyNoetherian S] in
/-- The module-iso transport respects the equivalence of quotients. -/
lemma congrModule_rel {V V' : S.Modules} (g : V ≅ V') {d : ℕ} {T : Over S}
    {x y : LocallyFreeQuotient V d T} (h : x.Rel y) :
    (congrModule g x).Rel (congrModule g y) := by
  obtain ⟨f, hf⟩ := h
  refine ⟨f, ?_⟩
  change (((Scheme.Modules.pullback T.hom).mapIso g).inv ≫ x.q) ≫ f.hom
    = ((Scheme.Modules.pullback T.hom).mapIso g).inv ≫ y.q
  rw [Category.assoc]
  exact congrArg (((Scheme.Modules.pullback T.hom).mapIso g).inv ≫ ·) hf

end LocallyFreeQuotient

/-- **Invariance of the Grassmannian functor under isomorphism of the
classified module**: an isomorphism `g : V ≅ V'` of sheaves of modules on `S`
induces an isomorphism `Grass(V, d) ≅ Grass(V', d)` of the relative
Grassmannian functors.  Pure functoriality: the components transport a
quotient along `congrModule`, and naturality is the naturality of the
pullback pseudofunctor comparisons in the module variable. -/
noncomputable def Grassmannian.congrIso {S : Scheme.{u}} [IsLocallyNoetherian S]
    {V V' : S.Modules} (g : V ≅ V') (d : ℕ) :
    Scheme.Grassmannian V d ≅ Scheme.Grassmannian V' d :=
  NatIso.ofComponents
    (fun T => Equiv.toIso
      { toFun := Quotient.map (LocallyFreeQuotient.congrModule g)
          (fun _ _ h => LocallyFreeQuotient.congrModule_rel g h)
        invFun := Quotient.map (LocallyFreeQuotient.congrModule g.symm)
          (fun _ _ h => LocallyFreeQuotient.congrModule_rel g.symm h)
        left_inv := fun z => by
          induction z using Quotient.ind with
          | _ x =>
            refine Quotient.sound ⟨Iso.refl _, ?_⟩
            change ((((Scheme.Modules.pullback T.unop.hom).mapIso g.symm).inv ≫
                (((Scheme.Modules.pullback T.unop.hom).mapIso g).inv ≫ x.q))) ≫ 𝟙 _
              = x.q
            rw [Category.comp_id, ← Category.assoc]
            rw [show (((Scheme.Modules.pullback T.unop.hom).mapIso g.symm).inv ≫
                ((Scheme.Modules.pullback T.unop.hom).mapIso g).inv)
              = 𝟙 _ by
                rw [Functor.mapIso_inv, Functor.mapIso_inv, Iso.symm_inv,
                  ← Functor.map_comp, Iso.hom_inv_id, CategoryTheory.Functor.map_id]]
            exact Category.id_comp x.q
        right_inv := fun z => by
          induction z using Quotient.ind with
          | _ x =>
            refine Quotient.sound ⟨Iso.refl _, ?_⟩
            change ((((Scheme.Modules.pullback T.unop.hom).mapIso g).inv ≫
                (((Scheme.Modules.pullback T.unop.hom).mapIso g.symm).inv ≫ x.q))) ≫ 𝟙 _
              = x.q
            rw [Category.comp_id, ← Category.assoc]
            rw [show ((((Scheme.Modules.pullback T.unop.hom).mapIso g).inv ≫
                ((Scheme.Modules.pullback T.unop.hom).mapIso g.symm).inv))
              = 𝟙 _ by
                rw [Functor.mapIso_inv, Functor.mapIso_inv, Iso.symm_inv,
                  ← Functor.map_comp, Iso.inv_hom_id, CategoryTheory.Functor.map_id]]
            exact Category.id_comp x.q })
    (fun {T T'} ψ => by
      ext z
      induction z using Quotient.ind with
      | _ x =>
        change Quotient.mk _ (LocallyFreeQuotient.congrModule g
            (LocallyFreeQuotient.pullbackAlong ψ.unop x))
          = Quotient.mk _ (LocallyFreeQuotient.pullbackAlong ψ.unop
            (LocallyFreeQuotient.congrModule g x))
        refine Quotient.sound ⟨Iso.refl _, ?_⟩
        change (((Scheme.Modules.pullback T'.unop.hom).mapIso g).inv ≫
            (pullbackTriangleIso (Over.w ψ.unop) V).inv ≫
            (Scheme.Modules.pullback ψ.unop.left).map x.q) ≫ 𝟙 _
          = (pullbackTriangleIso (Over.w ψ.unop) V').inv ≫
            (Scheme.Modules.pullback ψ.unop.left).map
              (((Scheme.Modules.pullback T.unop.hom).mapIso g).inv ≫ x.q)
        rw [Category.comp_id, Functor.map_comp]
        rw [← Category.assoc, ← Category.assoc]
        refine congrArg (· ≫ (Scheme.Modules.pullback ψ.unop.left).map x.q) ?_
        -- naturality of the triangle comparison in the module variable at `g.inv`
        simpa only [pullbackTriangleIso, Iso.trans_inv, Iso.app_inv, Category.assoc,
          Functor.mapIso_inv, NatTrans.comp_app, Functor.comp_map]
          using ((Scheme.Modules.pullbackCongr (Over.w ψ.unop)).inv ≫
            (Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp ψ.unop.left T.unop.hom).inv).naturality g.inv)

/-!
# A presheaf with unique values is represented by the terminal object

This file supplies the categorical bridge that was missing between "a presheaf
`F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v` has exactly one element at every test object" and
"`F` is representable by the terminal object of `C`".

Mathlib `v4.31` has `CategoryTheory.Limits.hasTerminal_of_unique` (a `C`-object
`X` with `Unique (Y ⟶ X)` for every `Y` is terminal) and
`CategoryTheory.Limits.IsTerminal.ofUnique`, but **not** the presheaf-side
statement: from `Nonempty (F.obj T)` and `Subsingleton (F.obj T)` at every `T`,
build the natural bijection `(X ⟶ Y) ≃ F.obj (op X)` that
`Functor.RepresentableBy` is. Both sides of that bijection are singletons —
the left because `Y` is terminal, the right by hypothesis — so the bijection
and its naturality are `Subsingleton.elim`. Verified absent by search over
mathlib and both projects; the nearest hits (`hasTerminal_of_unique`,
`isTerminalEquivUnique`) are about representing objects, not represented
presheaves.

## Why it is worth a named declaration

`Functor.RepresentableBy` is *data* (a chosen `Equiv` per object, plus a
naturality equation), not a `Prop`. So even when a presheaf is manifestly a
subterminal-and-inhabited functor, producing the `RepresentableBy` witness
still requires building that `Equiv` by hand at every use site. This file does
it once, at full categorical generality, so a consumer that has proved
`Nonempty` and `Subsingleton` pointwise gets the representability witness by a
single application — no `Equiv` plumbing.

## The intended consumer

`Picard/DivFamilyZero.lean` proves `Nonempty ((DivFunctorDeg π 0).obj (op T))`
for every `π` and test `T` (`DivFunctorDeg.instNonemptyObjZero`, the empty
divisor). If a lane proves the matching
`Subsingleton ((DivFunctorDeg π 0).obj (op T))` — that the empty divisor is the
*only* relative effective divisor of degree `0` — then
`representableByTerminal` yields
`(DivFunctorDeg π 0).RepresentableBy (Over.mk (𝟙 S))` immediately, the first
genuine `RepresentableBy` producer on the AJC divisor side. That `Subsingleton`
is real content (a fact about `fiberDeg`, a `finrank` with a junk value at
infinite dimension), and it is **not** discharged here; this file supplies only
the categorical interface it plugs into.

Everything here is about an arbitrary category and carries no algebraic-geometry
hypothesis; nothing closes any `sorry`.
-/

universe w v u

namespace CategoryTheory.Functor

variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C]

/-- **A presheaf that is pointwise nonempty and subsingleton is represented by
any terminal object.**

The representing map `(X ⟶ Y) ≃ F.obj (op X)` sends every morphism to the
unique element of `F.obj (op X)` and back to the unique morphism `X ⟶ Y` (which
exists because `Y` is terminal). Both round trips, and the naturality square,
are forced by the two `Subsingleton`s.

This is the presheaf-side companion of `Limits.hasTerminal_of_unique`, which is
absent from mathlib `v4.31`. -/
noncomputable def representableByTerminal (F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type w) {Y : C}
    (hY : Limits.IsTerminal Y)
    (hne : ∀ T : Cᵒᵖ, Nonempty (F.obj T)) (hss : ∀ T : Cᵒᵖ, Subsingleton (F.obj T)) :
    F.RepresentableBy Y where
  homEquiv {X} := by
    haveI := hne (Opposite.op X)
    haveI := hss (Opposite.op X)
    exact
      { toFun := fun _ => Classical.arbitrary _
        invFun := fun _ => hY.from X
        left_inv := fun _ => hY.hom_ext _ _
        right_inv := fun _ => Subsingleton.elim _ _ }
  homEquiv_comp {X X'} f g := by
    haveI := hss (Opposite.op X)
    exact Subsingleton.elim _ _

/-- **The `Unique`-packaged form of `representableByTerminal`.** When the values
of `F` are literally `Unique` (a single default plus subsingleton), the same
terminal object represents it. -/
noncomputable def representableByTerminal_of_unique (F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type w) {Y : C}
    (hY : Limits.IsTerminal Y) (h : ∀ T : Cᵒᵖ, Unique (F.obj T)) :
    F.RepresentableBy Y :=
  representableByTerminal F hY (fun T => ⟨(h T).default⟩) (fun T => (h T).instSubsingleton)

/-- **Existence corollary**: a pointwise nonempty-and-subsingleton presheaf is
representable (forgets the chosen terminal object). -/
theorem isRepresentable_of_terminal (F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type w) {Y : C}
    (hY : Limits.IsTerminal Y)
    (hne : ∀ T : Cᵒᵖ, Nonempty (F.obj T)) (hss : ∀ T : Cᵒᵖ, Subsingleton (F.obj T)) :
    F.IsRepresentable :=
  (representableByTerminal F hY hne hss).isRepresentable

      "body": "A --summary WRITE IS A SILENT DESTRUCTIVE EDIT, AND THE TOOL'S OWN OUTPUT CANNOT SHOW IT. Check the commit STAT, not the command's success line.\n\nWHAT HAPPENED (pic-c, AJCR 0092 r1). I claimed a row with roadmap set --owner --status --summary. The CLI printed 'Updated roadmap item' and nothing else. The commit stat then read 46 insertions / 117 DELETIONS. --summary REPLACES; the 117 lines were review-ajcr's rank-elevation analysis of that exact fork, TWO author self-retractions inside it, and the row's stated live target. I had read the row earlier in the session, but through roadmap list, which truncates -- so I never saw the body I was about to overwrite.\n\nWHY THE EXISTING LESSONS DO NOT COVER IT. The workspace has roadmap-yaml-edit-reverts-owner (a prose edit writing a stale OWNER over a live claim) and several items about staged deletions of other lanes' FILES. This is neither: the owner field was fine, no file was staged D, the write was to a row I legitimately hold, and the loss was entirely inside one YAML string. Every file-level check passes.\n\nTHE RULE, cheap and it is the only one that works. After any roadmap set --summary, read the commit stat. A deletion count above a handful means you replaced prose you never read. Recover with git show <commit>^:<path>, merge the prior summary verbatim, append yours behind a marker saying what happened, and re-verify a distinctive phrase from the old text is present.\n\nTHE SHARPER POINT. The destroyed text contained a retraction whose lesson was 'a probe with the hypothesis as a BINDER measures the conversion, so the control looks audited' -- i.e. I deleted a warning about exactly the class of error a reviewer had just caught me making elsewhere in the same session. Board prose is where a lane's corrections live, and it is the least protected thing in the workspace: no build breaks, no test fails, no file appears deleted.",

      "body": "DUPLICATION, DivisorFamilyDegreeZeroUnique.lean: the headline \"the FIRST inhabitant of DivFamZar at ANY parameter\" is FALSE over a field, and the uniqueness proof re-derives what two landed quotient-level lemmas already give.\n\nINHABITATION WAS NOT FIRST. exists_divFam_divFamDivisor_eq (DivisorFamilyFieldSurj.lean:143, the landed B-3 hsurj) at D = 0 gives a DivFam C K pi 0 with divFamDivisor = 0, hence DivFamZar C K pi 0 via toZar; divFamFieldEquiv.symm (0, le_rfl, by simp) gives the same class directly, and Quotient.out of it gives a CertifiedDivisorFamily C K pi 0. VERIFIED in a probe importing ONLY DivisorFamilyFieldSurj + DivSchemeAbel, no pic-c file, lake env lean EXIT=0. The correct claim is narrower and still worth having: trivZar is the first inhabitant at a GENERAL TEST RING R, where no field-surjectivity route applies.\n\nUNIQUENESS RE-DERIVES A LANDED LEMMA. presentationDivisor_eq_zero_of_isCertified_zero + divEq_of_isCertified_zero (:103, :114) work per-adaptation and then re-run divEq_of_presentationDivisor_eq.       "body": "REPLACING A HAND-ROLLED HYPOTHESIS BY 'THE STANDARD ONE' CAN STRENGTHEN IT INTO FALSITY -- and the test is a REFUTATION probe at the intended object, not a satisfiability witness.\n\nMEASURED (pic-e, AJC 0095 r7). I built the vocabulary the project was missing (graded prime avoidance => FiniteInAffine for projective schemes, all sorry-free), then restated the seam's antecedent with IsProjective of the representing scheme in place of the elementary FiniteInAffine, and committed 'entirely in standard vocabulary, no condition invented in this project'. I ran THREE vacuity checks and all three PASSED: the new conjunct is satisfiable (Spec k is projective over itself), it is NOT free (exact? fails at an arbitrary object), and the new antecedent does not close hypothesis-free. A fresh-context audit then refuted it in one step.\n\nWHY THE CHECKS MISSED IT. Every one of them asks 'could this hypothesis hold SOMEWHERE?'. None asks 'does it hold AT THE OBJECT THE STATEMENT IS ABOUT?'. IsProjective over a field forces IsProper, hence UniversallyClosed, hence CompactSpace over the compact Spec k -- and Pic_{C/k} is a disjoint union over deg in Z, so it is not quasi-compact.     58	/-- The canonical base-change map for the pushforward of a sheaf of modules.
    59	
    60	Given a commutative square
    61	```
    62	  X' --g'--> X
    63	  |f'        |f
    64	  v          v
    65	  S' --g---> S

    71	```
    72	  f_* F --f_*(unit)--> f_* (g')_* (g')^* F

    76	equalities are the pseudofunctoriality of pushforward together with the
    77	commutativity of the square.
